title: Staining 3D Broccoli-Based Scaffolds for Microstructure Visualization
author: Catherine A. Sword

steps.title: Prepare Scaffolds for Staining
steps.instruction: Transfer the desired number of scaffolds to a cover-glass-bottomed dish or chamber (e.g., Ibidi 80807).

substeps.instruction: Note: Plastic dishes such as well plates may be used, but they produce higher background fluorescence and are generally not compatible with microscope objectives > 10x.

steps.title: Apply Staining Reagents
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µl each of Calcofluor White (Honeywell Fluka Catalog #18909) and 10% w/v potassium hydroxide (Acros Organics Catalog #42414) onto each scaffold.

steps.title: Incubate Scaffolds
steps.instruction: Incubate the scaffolds at room temperature for at least 10 minutes to allow the stain to penetrate and bind to the scaffold.

steps.title: Rinse and Hydrate Scaffolds
steps.instruction: Rinse the scaffolds once with deionized water and add enough deionized water to keep them hydrated without allowing them to float above the dish/well surface.

steps.title: Image Scaffolds
steps.instruction: Transfer the dish/chamber/plate to an inverted fluorescence microscope and examine using settings similar to those used for DAPI.

substeps.instruction: For widefield microscopes: use 392/22 nm excitation and 447/60 emission filters.
For laser scanning confocal microscopes: excite with a 405 nm laser and collect emission in the range 425-441 nm.
